newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen up, affected by fall in IRS rates.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen up, affected by fall in IRS rates.

text.p: The key September Euroyen futures contract ended up on Tuesday, affected by a fall in interest rate swap (IRS) rates.
A foreign financial institution was said to have received fixed interest rates in the seven- to 10-year zone, a trader for an agricultural financial institution said.
Seven- to 10-year IRS rates fell about 6 basis points from the previous day, a trader for a long-term credit bank said.
The foreign financial institution most aggressively received nine-year fixed interest rates, the second trader added.
Traders said Euroyen futures also received upward momentum from a rise on SIMEX during the previous day.
"Large-lot purchases of Euroyen futures were seen on SIMEX last night, " the first trader said.
Some traders said Euroyen futures were supported by a rise in Japanese government bonds.
The March JGB futures contract closed at 125.62, up from the previous day's 125.30.
The Bank of Japan injected a net 200 billion yen into the money market this morning, maintaining its neutral stance.
Traders said the overnight call rate was traded most heavily at 0.48 percent, which they said was likely to be the weighted average on Tuesday.
The weighted average of the overnight call rate on Monday was 0.48 percent.
More trades at 0.49 percent were seen on Tuesday than on Monday, traders said.
A trust bank trader said the overnight call rate may rise slightly on Wednesday.
No new key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued on Tuesday.
The three-month CDs were tagged with a sell quote of 0.50 percent.
About 10 billion yen worth of two-month CDs were issued at 0.50 percent. One-month CDs were tagged with a sell quote of 0.50 percent.
Traders said they expected the Federal Open Market Committee to announce no changes in monetary policy at Tuesday's meeting. Tokyo Treasury Desk: 81-3 3432-8676
